fields.meta_title: RSVP Form Builder for Any Event | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an RSVP form that counts plus-ones, caps seats with a waitlist, and lets guests change a reply from their own link. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an RSVP Form That Counts Plus-Ones and Caps Seats
fields.hero_description: Build an RSVP form that counts every yes and plus-one, closes at your cap, and saves each reply to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After a Guest Says Yes
fields.features_subheading: The count on the reply-by date is what an RSVP form is for. Emergent builds the form and the guest list behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Plus-ones counted in the total

Decide which guests may bring someone. A yes with a plus-one adds two to the headcount, and the companion's name goes on the same reply, so the door list matches the count.
fields.feature_2:
A seat cap that starts a waitlist

Set the number of seats the room holds. Once that many guests say yes, later replies join a waitlist in order, and a guest who backs out frees a seat for the next one.
fields.feature_3:
Replies guests can change themselves

Each guest gets a personal link to their own reply. A guest can switch from yes to no or fix a misspelled name, and the host never has to edit the list by hand when plans change.
fields.feature_4:
Follow-up questions only for a yes

Ask about allergies or arrival time only after a yes. Guests who decline answer one question and leave, and the host reads the follow-up answers as totals per question.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before the reply-by date

Pick a reply-by date and when to nudge the quiet ones. The app emails guests who have not answered, and on the deadline it sends the host the final count of who is coming.
fields.feature_6:
The guest list stays in your database

Every reply is a row in a database you own, with no response cap. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, so next year's event can start from this one.

fields.usecase_heading: One RSVP Form, Four Kinds of Guest List
fields.tab_content_1:
Every yes and every plus-one adds up to 117

Tamsin Hoek sends the holiday party invitation to all 142 people at Strandquist Freight. By the Dec 5 reply-by date, 96 have said yes, 31 have said no, and 15 never replied. Of the 96, 21 are bringing a plus-one, and each of those counts as 2 people. That morning the app emails Tamsin a headcount of 117 for the caterer.
fields.tab_content_2:
Ilse's No hands her seat to the first name on the waitlist

Dovecote Arts Center can fit 80 members in the gallery for its preview night. The form took 80 yeses, then put the next 9 replies on a waitlist. When Ilse Faraji changes her reply to No from her own link, her seat goes to Orrin Ingrisch, first in line. He gets a confirmation email, and 8 people are still waiting.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 14 yeses, 2 come with a nut allergy

Pip turns 8 at Crestline Climbing, and Ines Duvernay-Pike invites 18 kids from her class. By the weekend, 14 say yes, 3 say no, and 1 has not answered. Each yes is asked about food allergies and whether a parent will stay. Before she orders the cake, Ines sees 2 nut allergies, 1 dairy allergy, and 5 parents staying.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who sits in the last 2 seats at table 12?

Saltmeadow Food Bank fills its gala by the table, and each table host names the guests in their seats. Constance Ferreira-Ng hosts table 12 and has named 6 of her 8 guests. On Oct 23, a week before the Oct 30 seating deadline, the app emails her a link to name the last 2. Each name she adds goes onto the seating chart.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an RSVP Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an RSVP form that keeps an accurate headcount from the first reply to the reply-by date, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide who may bring a guest
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 List the questions that follow a yes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a reply-by date and print it on the invitation itself. The form closes on that date, and the count you get that morning is the one you order food and chairs against. Leave a few days after it before the event for late changes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose whether every invitee gets a plus-one or only some do. For a partial list, mark those names before the form goes out. Write the rule in one line, such as one guest each for staff and none for contractors.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Find the number of people the room holds and subtract staff and speakers. That is your cap. Decide whether replies past it join a waitlist or see a message that the event is full, and how fast a released seat should move.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the first screen to one question: coming or not. Put food allergies and arrival time behind the yes. A guest who declines then finishes in seconds, and the follow-up answers come back only from people who will be there.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with the event name, the reply-by date, the plus-one rule, the cap, and the follow-up questions. Emergent builds the RSVP form, the guest list behind it, and a dashboard with every reply and the running headcount.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick when guests who have not answered hear from you, such as 7 days and 2 days before the reply-by date. Have the app email you the headcount on the deadline, with the waitlist shown on its own below it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Reply to your own invitation twice
fields.howto_step_7_des: Say yes with a plus-one under a test name and check that the headcount goes up by 2. Then open the personal link from the confirmation and change the reply to no. The count should drop by 2, and a waitlisted test guest should move up.

faq_plan.a: An RSVP form is an invitation's reply card, put online. Each guest answers whether they will come, and the host sees a running count of yes, no, and no reply. A fuller version also asks about food allergies or arrival time once a guest says yes.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an RSVP form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the event to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt: the reply-by date, who may bring a guest, the seat cap, and the questions to ask after a yes. Emergent builds the form and a page with the headcount, and the app saves each response as a row. Change any rule later by asking in plain English.

faq_plan.ref: Can you provide an example of an RSVP form?

prov.original: Can you provide an example of an RSVP form?

faq_plan.a: Yes. Here is one for a neighborhood block party. The first question asks whether you will come, yes or no. A yes then asks for your name, how many people are in your group, and whether you can bring a dish to share. The form closes on the reply-by date printed at the top.

faq_plan.q: What to include in a RSVP form?
faq_plan.ref: What to include in a RSVP form?

prov.original: What to include in a RSVP form?

faq_plan.a: Include the guest's name, a yes or no, the reply-by date, and an email address for the confirmation. Add a plus-one question only if guests may bring someone, and save the follow-up questions for people who say yes. Keep mailing addresses on a separate guest list form, since the RSVP should ask only what changes with the answer.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead of the date should an event RSVP form close?
faq_plan.a: Close it 2 or 3 days before the date your caterer or venue needs a final count, which leaves time to chase late replies. Ask both for that date before you write the invitation, and print the reply-by date on it. The app can email guests who have not replied in the days before the form closes.

faq_plan.q: What should I change in an RSVP form template before sending it?
faq_plan.a: Change the closing date, the follow-up questions, and the plus-one rule first, because a generic template cannot know them. Then delete every field you will not act on. With Emergent you describe those rules in a prompt instead of editing a template, and every reply lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a free RSVP form take unlimited replies?
faq_plan.a: Yes, on Emergent. The free tier covers building and publishing, and forms built with Emergent have no response caps. For a wedding, where one household replies for several people and picks meals, the wedding rsvp page covers those parts.

faq_plan.q: How do guests change their answer on an RSVP form after replying?
faq_plan.hint: How to create an online RSVP form?
faq_plan.a: They open a personal link from their confirmation email, which shows their own reply. From there a guest can switch yes to no or add or drop a plus-one, and the headcount moves with the change. Without that link, the guest has to email the host, who then edits the list by hand.

faq_plan.q: How should I share an RSVP form with guests?
faq_plan.a: Put the link in the invitation email, or print it as a QR code on a paper invitation. Send each guest a personal link when plus-ones are limited to certain names or replies need to be changeable. A single shared link suits an open event that anyone on the invitation list can forward.

faq_plan.q: Should a ticketed event use an RSVP form?
faq_plan.a: No. When guests pay for a ticket or pick a time slot, use an event booking form instead. An RSVP form records whether an invited guest is coming, and a booking form records what each person bought or reserved.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (SurveyMonkey, Jotform, Typeform, Canva), RSVP tools and a Reddit thread asking for a free RSVP link: every result helps a host collect a yes or a no, and none shows what happens to the count after that. This page covers the general event RSVP (office parties, member previews, kids' birthdays, charity galas) and the parts that keep a headcount right: plus-ones counted in the total, a seat cap with a waitlist, replies guests can change from their own link, follow-up questions that appear only after a yes, and table hosts who name their own guests. Wedding household lookups and meal choices stay on the wedding RSVP page, and paid or timed signups go to the event booking form.
